observation: Heading structure differs. The original has no h1, and its outline is just two h2s ('What's new at Great Day Improvements', 'HOME IMPROVEMENT RESOURCE CENTER'). The AI-built page has one h1, then five h2 section titles, with h3 card titles nested under them and an h4 in the footer.
The AI-built hero opens with a large 48px bold h1 in dark slate (rgb 31,42,51). It wraps to four left-aligned lines. The original has no h1 headline text at all.

Landmark markup differs. The original has no HTML5 landmarks and is built from 148 divs, 101 spans and 104 anchors. The AI-built page has a header, a nav, a main, four sections and a footer, with only 15 divs. Neither page uses article, aside or figure.

The page title differs. The original uses a keyword-style title, 'Home Improvement & Additions Contractors | Great Day Improvements'. The AI-built page uses a brand/product title, 'Great Day Improvements – Patio Enclosures® Sunrooms & Stanek Windows'.
The html lang attribute is empty on the original and set to 'en' on the AI-built page. Neither page has JSON-LD blocks.

Head and asset loading differs. The original loads 28 scripts and 7 stylesheets and has 13 meta tags, including msvalidate and google-site-verification. The AI-built page has no scripts, no external stylesheets and one inline style block, with only 3 meta tags (charset, viewport, description).

Container width differs. The original is a fixed centered column of about 980px on the 1440px canvas, with a left ribbon sidebar beside the main column. The AI-built page uses a single container of about 1060px with 190px side margins, and all section headers and grids align to it.
Layout technique differs. The original uses floats or positioning, with 1 flex container and no grid. The AI-built page uses 12 flex and 5 grid containers.

The header differs. The original has a large 215x130 logo on the left, three small brand logos separated by a divider, and a yellow-orange tab hanging from the top edge. The AI-built header is a white 80px bar with a thin bottom border, a small logo on the left and right-aligned nav links.

Logo placement differs. The original shows its logo large in the header (215x130). The AI-built page uses a small header logo (96x59), reuses it in a brand card (115x70), and shows a larger 300x181 version in the hero.

The main navigation differs. The original has a dark-blue band below the header with six small white links (Products & Services, Photo Gallery, Home Improvement Tips, About Us, Specials, Customer Service) and no nav element. The AI-built page puts four text links plus a phone-number button in a nav element inside the white header.

The original's yellow header panel holds a script 'Improve your home today!' line, a phone number, a blue 'Schedule Your FREE In-Home Design Consultation' button and a 'Find Your Location' zip input. The AI-built page has no consultation-scheduling CTA and no location lookup.

Form controls differ. The original has 1 button element, 1 form and 30 inputs (the zip lookup is the visible one), and its CTAs are mostly links styled as buttons. The AI-built page has no button elements and no form, and its CTAs are anchors.

The hero differs. The original is a horizontal rotator of five 676x301 image slides with text baked in, overlaid by a translucent bar reading 'Sunrooms | Windows | Doors | And More'. The AI-built hero is a static two-column split: an h1, a paragraph and two buttons on the left, and the logo image on the right, with no photographic hero.

The same hp-rotator 676x301 banner images, with their baked-in text, are used differently. The original shows them as full-size hero slides. The AI-built page shrinks and crops them to 335x149 as Explore card thumbnails with empty alt text.

The original has a pale-blue left sidebar ribbon with a notched bottom and drop shadow. It holds a house illustration, bullet lists grouped by brand logo, dotted dividers, and a yellow 'Book Your FREE No Obligation In-Home Consultation' box with a 'Schedule Now' button. The AI-built page has no sidebar.
The AI-built page has an 'Our brands' section: a three-column grid of equal bordered white cards. Each card centers a logo, a bold brand name and a muted subline, and the whole card is one anchor.

Image-based headings differ in extent. The original renders most headings and labels as raster images or script lettering ('Our Products & Services', 'Get Inspired!', 'Have questions?', 'Corporate Office', 'Site Map', 'Back to top'). The AI-built page uses live text headings, and only the 'Corporate Office' label remains a script-lettered PNG.

Font families differ. The original is set in Arial (345 elements) plus Helvetica Neue W01 webfonts (55 Roman on 104 elements, 75 Bold on 6). The AI-built page uses a single system-ui stack for all 116 text elements.
Body type differs. The original body is 16px with line-height 'normal' and black text. The AI-built body is 17px with a 27.2px (1.6) line-height in dark slate (rgb 31,42,51).
H2 styling differs. The original h2s are 21px at weight 400, and the 'What's new' heading is blue with only 'What's new' in bold. The AI-built h2s are 30.4px at weight 700.

Section intros differ. The original sets its 'What's new' heading between dotted horizontal rules. The AI-built page opens every section with a left-aligned bold h2 followed by a one-line muted subtitle.

Secondary text color differs. The original sets its intro and secondary copy in small grey rgb(77,79,81), used on 106 elements, in a narrow column about 620px wide with a superscript registered mark. The AI-built page uses a muted grey rgb(90,103,114) for subtitles, on 7 elements.

The palettes differ. The original is dominated by a mid blue (74,144,231), a pale blue (209,228,242), a navy (22,93,159) and a cream (244,232,218), with dark-blue links (4,63,118), and its yellow-orange comes from images. The AI-built page uses white and pale blue-grey (243,246,248) backgrounds, a deep blue accent (11,92,142) and a CSS amber CTA color (232,163,23).

Page backgrounds differ. The original body is transparent over a sky-blue to white vertical gradient, with decorative swirls beside the hero. The AI-built page has a white body, and its sections alternate between tinted and white bands.

Both pages close with a dark navy block. The original's block has a radial glow behind a script 'Back to top' label with an orange roof-shaped line. The AI-built footer is a plain dark navy band (rgb 20,32,42) with light grey text.

Both pages show two side-by-side promo image tiles: a silver/grey 'New financing options' tile and a blue 'SAVE BIG' tile with the phone number baked in. The original shows them at 284x194. The AI-built page shows them at 366x250 in a row spanning about two-thirds of the container.

The original has a 'Home Improvement Resource Center' banner (a wood-textured image with a hammer) on a cream rounded panel. The panel holds a 3x2 grid of article cards with 191x136 photos. The AI-built page has no resource center or article cards.

Both pages use linked cards whose title ends with a blue right-pointing arrow, and the whole card is the link. The original's cards are how-to articles (e.g. 'How Much Insulation Do I Need In My Attic?') with pale-blue caption strips in a 3x2 grid. The AI-built Explore cards are product categories in a 3-column grid of five, which leaves an empty slot, and their heights vary (240px vs 211px).
The original has two glossy blue button images, 'Ideas & Tips Blog' and 'View Photo Gallery', with chevrons, subtext and reflected shadows. The AI-built page has no blog or gallery buttons.

Both pages repeat a phone number as the recurring call to action. The original uses two different numbers, 800-230-8301 in the header and 888-468-0700 in the 'Have questions?' block. The AI-built page uses 888-468-0700 in the header button, the hero and the Call section.

The contact block differs. The original's 'Have questions?' block uses a yellow speech-bubble graphic, a script title image and a bold 'Call Us Today at 888-468-0700' line. The AI-built page has a two-column Call/Visit section with an h2 and an oversized (about 32px) bold blue phone link on the left and an address on the right.
Opening hours differ. The original lists them as small text. The AI-built page uses a real table of day/time pairs (3 rows, 6 cells) with right-aligned times, hairline row dividers and no header row.

The original footer has a Site Map of underlined text links in three columns (brands, gallery/blog/specials/about, customer service), next to the Corporate Office address block. The AI-built page has no site map.

Contractor license numbers differ. The original shows them as a dense run-on fine-print block. The AI-built page uses a single ul of 17 items in three columns, in small light-grey text (201,211,218) under a bold h4.
Both footers show the accreditation badges (Energy Star, EPA Lead-Safe, remodeler awards) as a single 366x47 raster image. The AI-built page places it on a white rounded plate inside the dark footer.
On the AI-built page, the alt text of the footer badge strip names three brand logos, while the image shows certification badges.
Both footers end with a copyright line that credits the web agency. On the AI-built page the credit is a white underlined link.
The original uses recurring blue or grey dotted-line dividers between the intro and 'What's new', under the promo tiles and between sidebar brand groups. The AI-built page has no dotted dividers.

Corner rounding differs. The original is almost entirely square (443 elements at 0, 12 at 1–7px, none at 8px or more). The AI-built page has 102 elements at 0, 4 at 1–7px and 10 at 8–15px, on cards and the badge plate. Neither page uses 16px+ radii or pills.

The primary button differs. On the original it is 'Accept and Close', probably a cookie banner: navy (22,93,159) with white text, a 5px radius and 9px 12px 11px padding. On the AI-built page it is 'Our story': amber (232,163,23) with dark text, a 6px radius and 12px 24px padding, paired with an outlined blue 'Call today' button.

Depth and effects differ. The original is skeuomorphic: bevels, ribbons, a wood texture, metallic gloss and reflections are baked into images, with 1 CSS box-shadow and 2 gradients. The AI-built page is flat, with no box-shadows or gradients, and gets its depth from thin borders and background tints.
Neither page uses CSS animations, transforms or backdrop blur.
Transition counts differ: 111 elements on the original declare CSS transitions, against 10 on the AI-built page.

Class usage differs, though neither page uses Tailwind-like naming. The original has 371 class uses across 107 unique names plus 82 inline style attributes. The AI-built page has 35 class uses across 17 names and 1 inline style attribute.

Image use differs, though neither page has inline SVGs. The original has 25 images, with 3 missing alt text and some decorative thumbnails using empty alt. The AI-built page has 14 images, none missing alt, but 7 content and promo images have empty alt.
ARIA use is sparse on both pages but differs: 7 elements on the original, 1 on the AI-built page.

Copy differs. The original has 258 words and 2 emoji, and is marketing-led with repeated 'FREE' and 'No Obligation' calls to action. The AI-built page has 198 words, no emoji, and short informational copy. Neither page uses exclamation marks or em dashes in DOM text.

Page length and density differ. The original is 2228px tall, with a crowded first screen and sparse empty areas lower down. The AI-built page is 3126px tall, with generous vertical whitespace (about 56px padding above each h2 and sections 420–700px tall).
